note: UTE G1 per-family retirement ledger. The four terms are the owner's predicate (RetireAllowed = OldBaseline AND NewPathVerified AND SemanticDifferencesResolved AND NegativeControlsPass). A row's state is a MIRROR of the computed verdict, never a substitute for it: scripts/ute-retirement-gate.mjs re-reads every `evidence.path`, refuses files git does not track, and refuses files that do not contain the claimed verdict token. 'SemanticDifferencesResolved' is not byte equality: every difference with blocking:true must carry an owner approval whose `record` is itself a committed file naming the approver (docs/plans/memo/ute-g1-20261120/RETIREMENT.md). Seeded 2026-11-20 by UTE-0; fs is NOT_RETIREABLE because both recorded semantic differences are retirement-blocking and neither has an approved compatibility interface.

oldBaseline.note: 10 (request -> effect) vectors captured on the legacy governed route-C seam (mountMemberA5sfRealm + attachA5sfNativeToolModules) on host 0.2.0-rc.2 @ 639ed01539; fixture identity in the sibling golden/old-path.meta.txt. This is the OldBaseline term for the FS family only — it says nothing about any other family.

newPathVerified.note: Prototype provider + the pinned next host's own ToolsService.execute; 10/10 vectors green on rc.5. This proves the PROTOTYPE path only: it is not a live boot, it does not prove read confinement (CLAIM_NOT_OBSERVABLE), and it must never be cited as a safety verdict.

differences.summary: old path FS_SANDBOX_DENIED vs new path FS_PERMISSION_DENIED (rc.5 tool-fs sandbox.ts:139-143 dereferences policy.mode); retirement needs the owner-approved compatibility interface: adopt the fs-sandbox protocol (sandboxMode + sandbox-policy) or keep a non-sandbox code and accept different model-facing refusal text.

old path refuses in prose, new path in typed FsError codes; the corpus compares a closed refusal CLASS vocabulary. Code-level equality would need the old path to emit codes; that is a semantic change and must be owner-approved before switching.

semanticDifferencesResolved.note: Both recorded differences are retirement-blocking=YES and neither has an approval record, so this term is FALSE today by construction, not by opinion. The same two facts are printed on every prototype run as SEMANTIC-DIFF lines and asserted by tests/ute-g1-fs/lane-suite.test.mjs.

negativeControlsPass.note: NC-1 lane bites, NC-2 harness bites on a mutated golden cell, NC-3 no legacy fallback (typed NextHostMissingError), NC-4 the lane is load-bearing. These are the negative controls for the FS prototype claims; per-family retirement must re-run the family's own controls (a green FS control is not evidence for Web or PTY).

families.note: FS is the first family in the UTE G1 ordering and may retire before Web/PTY (owner ruling: per-family retirement is incremental). It may not retire today: the semantic-difference term is false and the gate refuses with UTE_SEMANTIC_DIFFERENCES_UNRESOLVED.
